stem: An adult has a markedly elevated alkaline phosphatase (ALP). Which interpretation is most appropriate?

options.A: Hepatobiliary and bone sources are common possibilities, and additional evaluation may be needed to identify the source
options.B: An elevated ALP can only originate from kidney disease
options.C: An elevated ALP always identifies one specific bone disorder
options.D: ALP has no relationship to hepatobiliary or skeletal conditions

rationale: Mayo Clinic Laboratories states that serum ALP is used in evaluation of hepatobiliary disease and bone disease associated with increased osteoblastic activity. ALP isoenzyme testing can help distinguish liver from bone sources. Therefore, an elevated ALP is not specific to a single organ or diagnosis.
educational_objective: Recognize common liver/biliary and bone sources of elevated alkaline phosphatase.
source_document_title: Alkaline Phosphatase, Total and Isoenzymes, Serum (ALKP)
source_claim_supported: Supports liver and bone as important sources of elevated ALP and use of isoenzymes to help localize the source.
correction_summary: Preserved the liver-versus-bone construct while removing a distractor set built around implausible kidney-only assumptions.
audit_findings: A is the clinically correct nonspecific interpretation; B-D falsely restrict or deny established ALP sources.
blueprint_locator: 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan, Reduction of Risk Potential, printed p.13 / PDF p.17
